newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-PACKERS RE-SIGN FREE AGENT DT GILBERT BROWN.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-PACKERS RE-SIGN FREE AGENT DT GILBERT BROWN.

text.p: The Super Bowl champion Green Bay Packers managed to hold onto one of their prized free agents by signing defensive tackle Gilbert Brown to a three-year contract, the team announced on Tuesday.
Brown, who turns 26 on Saturday, anchored the NFC's top-ranked defence against the run and helped the Packers win their first Super Bowl in 29 years.

The 6-2 (1.88 m), 325-pound (147 kg) Brown, who has been described by coach Mike Holmgren as "a guy-and-a-half wide," started all 16 games for Green Bay last season, playing a key role on a defensive unit that allowed a league-low 210 points.

The re-signing of Brown was a coup for General Manager Ron Wolf, who had made retaining the defensive lineman a high priority. Published reports last weekend had Brown on the verge of signing with the Jacksonville Jaguars.
Brown was extremely difficult to single-team, and double-teaming him often freed up fellow linemates such as veteran defensive end Reggie White.
Brown had 11 tackles in the post-season, including five in the 35-21 Super Bowl win over the New England Patriots. He also forced a fumble in the NFC Championship against Carolina.

Brown was one of 11 unrestricted free agents on the Packers. Return specialist Desmond Howard, the Super Bowl Most Valuable Player, and veteran receiver Don Beebe are among the team's other key free agents.
